cards.explanation: The answer is “Follow Me.” Jesus says it to Levi son of Alphaeus, the man sitting at the tax booth. Two words, no speech, no sales pitch. I've watched bakers take longer picking a cookie shape. And Levi got up and followed Him.

The answer is False. The text shows no request for time at all. Jesus says “Follow Me,” and Levi got up and followed Him. There's no gap in the story for thinking it over, friends. It goes straight from the call to the following.

The answer is many tax collectors and sinners. They were eating with Jesus and His disciples at Levi's house. The text adds that there were many who followed Him. Levi doesn't host a small dinner, friends, he hosts a FULL one.
The answer is scribes. At Levi's house, the scribes who were Pharisees see Jesus eating with tax collectors and sinners, and they have a question about it. Notice who the text says they ask, friends.

The answer is False. The scribes who were Pharisees don't ask Jesus Himself. They ask His disciples, “Why does He eat with tax collectors and sinners?” It's a question about Him, asked of the others. Then, on hearing this, Jesus tells them His answer.

The answer is the sick. Jesus says, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick.” He uses a picture everybody gets, because everybody knows why people go see a doctor. Then He says, “I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners.”

The answer is righteous. Jesus says, “I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners.” He says it right after, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick.” And it's His answer to the scribes who were Pharisees, who had asked His disciples why He eats with tax collectors and sinners.

The answer is True. John's disciples and the Pharisees were often fasting, so people came to Jesus and asked, “Why don’t Your disciples fast like John’s disciples and those of the Pharisees?” They bring the question straight to Him, friends. And He answers with a wedding.

The answer is while He is with them. Jesus says, “How can the guests of the bridegroom fast while He is with them? As long as He is with them, they cannot fast.” The bridegroom is right there with the guests, friends. So it's no time for fasting.

The answer is that He will be taken from them. Jesus says, “But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them…” The picture changes here, friends. First He says the guests cannot fast while He is with them, and then He looks ahead to a time still coming.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “…the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them; then they will fast.” First He says they cannot fast while the bridegroom is with them. Then He gives the time when they will, friends.

The answer is that the new piece pulls away and the tear gets worse. If someone sews a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment, Jesus says, “…the new piece will pull away from the old, and a worse tear will result.” So the fix makes things worse. I tie my apron with my mustache, but even I can follow that.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment.” It's something people don't do, friends. And He adds that if someone did, the new piece would pull away from the old, and a worse tear would result.

The answer is that the wine bursts the skins. Jesus says, “…no one pours new wine into old wineskins. If he does, the wine will burst the skins…” Old wineskins and new wine don't go together, friends. Then He tells what to do instead.
The answer is ruined. Jesus says the wine will burst the skins, “…and both the wine and the wineskins will be ruined.” Nobody comes out ahead, friends. Both are lost.
